sentences.text:
Mangali Paharin claiming herself descendant of the recorded tenant came to the writ Court with the prayer for payment of compensation, appointment to her by virtue of her lands being acquired by the Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL) and seeking cancellation of appointment offered to the respondent nos. 6 and 7.
4.

The writ Court has considered the rival claims in the following manner:
"7. I am of the considered view that the acquisition proceedings which was completed far back, cannot be reopened merely on the basis of order passed in M.P. Case No.
636 of 2011.
The petitioner has failed to show before this Court any illegality in the acquisition proceedings of the said land by the concerned authority.

8. It is the specific stand of the respondent-ECL that the recorded tenant of the said land had no heir and in support of the said contention, letter dated 13.07.2011 issued by the Circle Office, Boarijore has been brought on record.
Thus, the title of the petitioner upon the said land is disputed which cannot be adjudicated in the Writ Jurisdiction of this Court.

Otherwise also, though the law of limitation normally does not apply in the writ proceedings, yet several judicial pronouncements have been made from time-to-time that the delay, which is unexplained and inordinate, can be a ground to refuse the relief as claimed in the writ petition.

Moreover, Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (in short "the Act, 1894") specifically provides that if a person has any objection to the award, he may make application to the Collector for reference to the Court for deciding the objection whether the same is relating to the measurement of the land, the amount of compensation, the persons to whom it is payable, or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested.

The period of limitation for filing the said application is also provided in sub-section(2) of Section 18 of the Act, 1894 wherein it has been provided that if the objector was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, it is to be filed within six weeks from the date of the Collector's award and in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under Section 12 (2) of the Act, 1894, or within six months from the date of the Collector's award, whichever period shall first expire.
The petitioner has not been able to give sufficient explanation as to why she did not agitate the matter before the Collector within the said period of limitation.
9. Under the aforesaid facts and circumstances, I do not see any ground to entertain the prayers made by the petitioner in the writ petition.
The writ petition being devoid the merit is accordingly dismissed."

5. Against the order dated 17th October 2019 by which WP(C) No. 351 of 2014 has been dismissed,
the writ petitioner has approached this Court in the present Letters Patent Appeal.
6. There is no dispute as regards acquisition of lands comprised under Jamabandi No. 17 under the Coal Bearing Acquisition and Development Act, 1957.

The case pleaded by the respondents is that Mangali Paharin Aged About 42 Years vs The Union Of India Through Secretary on 7 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8434609/
2 the lands comprised under Jamabandi No. 17 belongs to Lakhiya Kaharin who died issueless and,
therefore, a Faut Case vide S.E. No. 135/77-78 was filed by Jagdish Malto who was the Pradhan of the village and the Court of Sub-Divisional Officer at Godda declared Jamabandi Jote lands as "faut".

This has also been brought on record that in Settlement Case No. 168/77-78, Cyril Malto was allotted the aforesaid lands comprised under Jamabandi No. 17 vide order dated 16th March 1979 and he came in possession over the said lands.
Latter on, Mutation Case No. 2/2005-2006 was allowed and correction slip was issued in favour of Prem Lata Malto.

7. On the basis of the aforesaid records, the respondents resisted the claim of the appellant on the ground that compensation for the subject lands has already been paid to the person concerned and appointment was given to the nominated persons.

From the pleadings by the appellant it appears that she has made an allegation that the respondent nos. 6 and 7 by forging documents in connivance with some government officials obtained illegal benefits and employment on the basis of the lands actually belonging to her.
Thus, the very basis of the writ petition was emanating from a dispute which could not have been adjudicated in a writ proceeding.

Whether the respondent nos. 6 and 7 have forged any document and the records of S.E. No. 135/77-78 and Mutation Case No.
2/2005-2006 have been procured in connivance with some government officials are the issues which can be conclusively decided by taking oral and documentary evidence in a civil Court of competent jurisdiction.

8. Having regard to the nature of the prayer made in WP(C) No. 351 of 2014, in our opinion, the writ Court has rightly refused to exercise its power under Article 226 of the Constitution of India and,
accordingly, LPA No. 321 of 2022 is dismissed.
